verdict_reason: Every declared finder and search constrains on organisationId and the index supports them, but the inherited MongoRepository CRUD leaves unscoped id-only methods on the interface and the two countryCode query paths have no cross-org test.

todos.issue: Extending MongoRepository<Address, String> publishes unscoped id-only CRUD (findById, deleteById, delete, existsById, findAll, deleteAll) alongside the org-scoped finders, so the tenant guard the class javadoc claims (cv-010) is a convention, not a constraint
todos.fix: Extend Repository<Address, String> and declare only what is used - save, the three org-scoped @Query searches, findByIdAndOrganisationId, findByOrganisationIdAndStatus (plus deleteAll for test cleanup) - so findById/deleteById are not on the interface at all

todos.issue: The 'organisationId': ?0 term is the only tenant guard in the hand-written searchByCountryCode and searchByQueryAndCountryCode queries, and neither has a cross-org test - AddressSearchIT seeds OTHER_ORG only in searchIsOrgScopedAndExcludesSoftDeleted, which exercises the q-only searchByQuery path
todos.fix: In AddressSearchIT, add an OTHER_ORG (and a DELETED) row to countryCodeParamMatchesStoredAlpha2Code and combinedQueryAndCountryCodeMatchesEitherTextOrCountryCode, asserting totalItems excludes them

todos.issue: The three @Query methods hard-code the string literal 'ACTIVE' for status while findByOrganisationIdAndStatus binds the AddressStatus enum, so the persisted status representation now has two sources of truth
todos.fix: Bind status as a parameter in the raw queries ('status': ?N) and pass AddressStatus.ACTIVE from OperatorService.queryPage, matching the derived method
